text:
Trevor Zegras keeps making headlines for the wrong reason. He sat for 10 minutes in a recent loss after a misconduct for tapping his stick at a referee, and the reporting around it says Rick Tocchet was not happy. It adds to a reputation he has been trying to shed since Anaheim.

The hockey has been mixed too. He has 14 points in 20 games, 8 on the power play, but at five on five the Flyers get just 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 9 points worse than without him. That is a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him 47th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement and driving play.

He is shooting 9.8% against a career norm closer to 13.7%, so the goals should come. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 55% of his entries, which is the skill Philadelphia wanted. Our projection is about 63 points. The question is how many more stick taps the coach will sit through.
headline: Zegras brings the skill and the headaches
